summary: Completed backend golden-path regression and frontend desktop/mobile smoke testing. Core login, role switching, navigation, methodology drawer, ingestion, PCF versioning, MRV lock, issuance, duplicate prevention, public valid/unknown API responses, and mobile overflow checks were exercised.

critical.issue: Before any passport is issued, the default identifier SAU-NSC-08-4F2A is accepted as valid because the comparison falls back to that hardcoded identifier while state.passport is null. The response has status valid with passport null.

ui_bugs.issue: Unknown/unverifiable passport page still renders a green VERIFIED status chip; this contradicts the displayed 'Passport not verifiable' state.

action_items: Return unverifiable when state.passport is null, regardless of requested identifier; remove the default-ID fallback from public verification.
Render the public status chip conditionally as VERIFIED only for valid results, otherwise UNVERIFIABLE or a neutral warning state.
Add data-testid attributes to remaining interactive controls such as company supplier review, manual emission entry, and ledger link if they are intended to be part of the demo flow.
critical_code_review_comments: Public verification currently exposes a false valid state before issuance, violating the required public passport warning/state behavior.
The in-memory global state is shared across sessions and test runs; this is acceptable for a prototype demo but makes reset/isolation impossible and can cause order-dependent verification results.

success_rate.backend: 50% (1 of 2 regression tests passed; full golden path passed)

seed_data_creation: No new seed data created; used the existing seeded demo accounts and Northstar dataset.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Core workflow was exercised successfully. Re-run public verification against an unissued state before testing issuance, then verify valid and duplicate issuance states. Unknown UI route currently shows correct message but incorrect VERIFIED badge.
rca of the issue: Backend /api/public/verify compares the requested ID to (state.passport or {}).get('id', 'SAU-NSC-08-4F2A'), so the demo identifier is treated as issued even when passport is null. PublicVerify independently hardcodes the VERIFIED chip instead of deriving it from result.status.
